chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Yahya, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Speech is of three types: truth, lie, and reconciliation between people.

It was said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the reconciliation between people?' He said: 'You hear speech from a man, which reaches him and makes his soul feel bad. Then you meet him and say, 'I heard from so-and-so that he said good things about you,' which is the opposite of what you actually heard from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of reconciliation between people in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes speech into truth, lie, and reconciliation (islah), defining the latter as strategically conveying a positive report opposite to what was heard to soothe feelings and resolve conflict. This concept, known as *islah* or *tadlis al-haqq* (veiling the truth for peace), is distinct from outright lying (*kidhb*) because the core message remains beneficial and non-deceptive in intent, serving as a practical tool for social harmony in Shia jurisprudence.
